First, note time zones in 1917 (pre-standardized offsets may vary, but using historical data):

- Australia/Sydney: AEST (UTC+10) or possibly AEDT? In 1917, Australia introduced daylight saving temporarily, but starting 1917-01-01? Actually, DST was first used in 1917 in Australia from Jan 1? Let's check: Historical records show Sydney introduced DST in 1917 starting on January 1, 1917, as a wartime measure, moving clocks forward 1 hour (so UTC+11). But August is winter in Australia — DST would not be in effect in August 1917. So likely standard time: UTC+10.

- Europe/Athens: In 1917, Greece likely used EET (UTC+2) year-round (no DST until later). Historical time zone database (IANA tzdata) says:  
  Before 1916-07-28, Athens was LMT (UTC+1:34:52).  
  From 1916-07-28, Greece adopted EET (UTC+2).  
  So in August 1917, Athens is UTC+2.

Thus:
Sydney time: 05:00 August 5, 1917 (UTC+10)  
Convert to UTC: 05:00 − 10 hours = 19:00 (previous day) August 4, 1917 UTC.  
Convert to Athens time: 19:00 UTC + 2 hours = 21:00 August 4, 1917.

FINAL_ANSWER: 21:00 August 4, 1917
